newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Klaus says Czech goods face barriers in EU markets.
newsitem.headline: Klaus says Czech goods face barriers in EU markets.

text.p: Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Thursday the Czech trade deficit with the European Unioon was partly due to trade barriers preventing Czech goods reaching EU markets.

Klaus told a news conference after talks with Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, whose country currently holds the six-month rotating EU presidency, that the Czech trade deficit with the EU was not just due to Czech goods ability to compete.

"I do not interpret the trade deficit only in terms of the capability of our economy to succeed in EU markets. I also think it is a result of existing barriers to our coming to the EU markets and also of large subsidies, especially in agricultural products," Klaus said.

The Czech trade deficit widened to 160.3 billion crowns in 1996 from 95.7 billion the previous year. The 1996 trade deficit with the EU was 125.0 billion crowns, compared with 59.2 billion the previous year.
The government has often blamed lower consumption in Germany for a stagnation of Czech exports.
The Czech Republic is seen as a leading contender to be among the first new members of both the EU and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
"Everybody sees that the Czech Republic will of course belong to the first group of countries that can become members of the European Union," Kok said.
